citations.F1: `serialize_event` runs one `SELECT ... FROM users` per event — 1,912 round trips per request on a pool of 10. Fix: one `WHERE id = ANY($1)` batch fetch
citations.F2: The dedupe loop is `if ev["dedupe_key"] in seen` against a list — O(n²), ~1.8M comparisons for acme. Fix: use a `set`
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` uses blocking `requests.get` inside an async handler, so each uncached IP freezes the whole event loop for up to 2 s ... Fix: async HTTP client (`httpx.AsyncClient`)
citations.F4: Add `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)` — no index on `org_id` exists, so the 1.4 s query scans 4.2M rows
citations.F5: `_request_timings` — an unbounded list appended once per request; at 120 req/s that is ~8.6M floats after 20 h. Fix: `collections.deque(maxlen=...)`
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is a second unbounded dict keyed by client IP with no eviction. Fix: bounded LRU with a TTL.
citations.F9: Do not ship the on-call proposal — 16 workers × 50 connections × 6 pods = 4,800 Postgres connections ... 4× the workers multiplies the per-process memory leak rather than fixing it ... Also reject the cache on its own terms
citations.F11: keyed on `(org_id, since, limit)` where `since` defaults to `now() - 30d` computed per request, every key is unique, so the hit rate is ~0
